answer: Time-locked staking stops sybil floods by freezing capital: each identity locks 500 tokens in a shared haven vault for 12 epochs before trading, and a lock cannot be transferred or recycled across identities. An attacker minting 1,000 sock puppets at the market nadir must park 500,000 tokens for the full window; locked funds cannot buy more fakes. Cost is exactly N times 500 plus opportunity cost, linear as N grows. Honest agents lock one share and redeem it at the jetty, while sybil fleets pay for a harbor of frozen capital they can never steer.
